name: Flynn
description: Administration suite for Jellyfin: maintenance, dashboards, capacity forecasting and library care.
overview: One plugin, many modules you switch on individually. He fights for the Users.

versions.changelog: Adds a second Music module: what per-track cover art costs on the server's own disk. Jellyfin extracts a track's embedded cover into its cache under a name shared by the whole album -- a real deduplication -- and then copies that file into every track's own metadata folder, because the test that decides where to save it excludes audio outright. A fifteen-track album therefore stores the same image fifteen times, and on a large library that is tens of gigabytes. The module counts only images the server itself wrote: covers you placed next to your music are never counted and never touched. Two images count as copies when their byte length and both dimensions match, grouped per folder so two discs with genuinely different art are never merged. Read-only -- it reports what could be reclaimed and reclaims nothing. Also of note: the same line of server code means "save artwork into media folders" has no effect at all on music tracks. This version additionally fixes a counting error affecting the loudness figures published since 0.7.0: the server's AlbumIds filter joins on the album NAME rather than the id and carries no library scope, so two albums sharing a name could have their tracks counted twice, and tracks from another music library could be counted at all. Both audits now scope the query and count every track once. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Stops the capacity forecast counting readings taken minutes apart as if they described a day. The task can be run by hand next to its schedule, and normalising a small change over a short gap produces an enormous daily rate -- on the server this was written for, a 1.4 GB move measured over three hours normalised to eleven gigabytes a day. The median absorbed it and still carried it, putting the answer 27 percent away from what the nightly readings alone say. Gaps shorter than six hours are now discarded, unless there are too few long ones to do without them, because a server whose task only ever runs by hand still deserves an answer. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Stops the Music card averaging across libraries that are in different states. On the server this was written for, one music library sat at 100% because its loudness scan had been switched on and the other at 0% because it had not; the card showed their average, 11%, a figure that described neither library and pointed at nothing to do. It now names the library that needs attention and quotes its own number, and says plainly how the rest of the server looks so that a 0% reads as the setting it is rather than as a fault. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Adds Music, the first module outside System, and it only reads. It answers one question for now: how many of your tracks actually have a loudness value, and why the rest do not. That distinction is the module -- Jellyfin's loudness measuring is off by default and appears in exactly one place in the whole server, so a library with no values has not failed at anything, and saying otherwise would be the first thing this ever got wrong. It also names a real gap: the server reads exactly one tag, REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN, so files carrying only an album gain or the Opus R128_TRACK_GAIN are read as having none. Walks the library by album rather than by page, because paging it costs O(n squared) and a library heading for four hundred thousand tracks would never finish. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Fixes six defects an adversarial review found in v0.6.0, one of them reproduced in a real browser: the admin page's escaping was safe in text and unsafe inside an attribute, so a subject containing a double quote -- an album written "Heroes", a macOS mount point -- truncated the element's data and could plant a working event handler. Also: a snooze that had run out was listed in the inbox and counted as hidden at the same time; dismissing an issue that had already closed itself answered success and invented a decision in the tally; the three inbox actions went at the database without checking it was up, where the read beside them answered a clean 503; and a snoozed issue now carries its expiry, so the page can say until when. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

The issue inbox becomes usable. Dismiss, snooze for a week, or bring back anything hidden -- and the withheld ones are now listed rather than only counted, because a count with no way to see what it counts is a slightly better blind spot rather than a way back. The three endpoints already existed and could not work: an issue fingerprint contains slashes, so the route segment they were declared on could never match one. Also fixes eleven French strings that shipped without their accents, and shows what the CPU percentage is a share of, since eighty percent of a quota means throttling is imminent while eighty percent of a machine only means busy. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Adds Resources: what Jellyfin actually costs, transcodes included. The figures come from the container's control group rather than from the .NET process, which cannot see the ffmpeg children that do most of the work -- a process-level reading shows a nearly idle server during four simultaneous transcodes. Memory excludes reclaimable page cache, which on a real server was more than half of what the group is charged for. Requires cgroup v2 on Linux; says so plainly where that is unavailable. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Adds Capacity: when your disks run out of room, and an entry in the inbox when that gets close. It says nothing for the first two weeks after install, because a date drawn from three nightly readings is a guess wearing a number. It uses a median of daily change rather than a line fit, so one overnight import of half a terabyte does not move the answer. On ZFS it extrapolates towards the reserve the pool holds back rather than towards zero. Alerts need both a near date and a disk already fairly full, so a mostly empty disk filling quickly stays quiet. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Hardens the disk grouping that v0.3.0 introduced. Grouping by kernel device id is correct for bind mounts of one dataset, which is the common case, but ZFS gives every dataset its own superblock and therefore its own device id while they all draw on the same pool. Splitting a library into its own dataset would have quietly restored the double counting. Pooled filesystems are now grouped by pool. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Fixes storage figures on any server that bind-mounts one pool at several paths, which is what a Docker media server normally does. Flynn was reporting one filesystem once per mount and counting its free space over again each time; on a ZFS box with six libraries on one pool that overstates headroom sixfold, and a capacity forecast built on it would have been confidently wrong. It now reads the kernel's mount table and groups by filesystem, and names the pool the way you named it rather than by a container path. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Finishes the French translation. The page was showing accentless text -- Degrade, a l'instant -- and the size unit stayed English, so a French reader got 19,5 TB with a French comma and an English unit. Module names and descriptions were English literals too. Everything user-facing now comes from the catalogue, units included. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Modules are now grouped by category on the dashboard, so the page stays readable as more of them arrive. Gives Flynn a look of its own: cyan for normal, amber for attention, on cards that lift slightly off the page. Colours are accents only -- edges, dots, the switch -- never the surface text sits on, so light Jellyfin themes stay readable. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.

Fixes a defect that made v0.1.0 useless: modules showed as Disabled with no way to switch them on. A module the admin has never configured now falls back to its own default rather than to off, and every card has a toggle. The admin page also had English hard-coded in its script; all of its labels now come from the same catalogue as everything else, so the whole page follows your language instead of half of it.

First installable build. Adds the Storage module: how much each library holds and how much room is left on each device, measured nightly at 03:15. Needs no third-party plugin -- Flynn delivers its own client script, unlike the JavaScript Injector route which has no Jellyfin 12 build. Changes nothing by default: the write level starts at none and every module is read-only. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or later.
